headline: High risk of data leakage and capability conflict: nullclaw’s broad workspace/network access can collide with agentic-flow’s shell/MCP/git actions.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: agentic-flow can use MCP, stdin/stdout, and background workers, while nullclaw exposes web, file, browser, and delegate surfaces. That creates a plausible instruction-smuggling path if nullclaw content is routed into agentic-flow’s parsers or MCP inputs. The pairwise bridge is documented only indirectly, so uncertainty pushes to medium.
conditions: IF nullclaw forwards web or workspace content into agentic-flow MCP/stdin without provenance checks, injection is possible.
IF agentic-flow parses file or MCP payloads as instructions, attacker-controlled text can steer tool use.
mitigations: Disable automatic ingestion of nullclaw outputs into agentic-flow prompts.
Add a provenance tag to every cross-agent message.
Require manual approval before MCP calls that originate from nullclaw content.
Use a read-only handoff file with a fixed schema.
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization and instruction/data separation at the orchestrator.

B_data_leakage.rationale: nullclaw explicitly touches API keys, private keys, bearer tokens, workspace files, and audit logs, while agentic-flow can execute shell, use MCP, and egress to allowlisted network destinations. If they share a workspace or hand off files, sensitive data can flow from nullclaw into agentic-flow and then out through its networked tools. The blast radius includes secrets and logs, so high is warranted.
conditions: IF both agents can read the same workspace files, secrets in nullclaw’s workspace become available to agentic-flow.
IF agentic-flow sends file contents through MCP or GitHub APIs, those secrets can leave the local boundary.
mitigations: Separate workspaces and mount agentic-flow read-only.
Move secrets out of shared directories immediately.
Disable network egress for agentic-flow during shared-file processing.
Rotate any keys that may already have been exposed.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent secret isolation and egress policy at the runtime layer.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents can execute shell, install packages, modify git state, spawn subprocesses, and use MCP. agentic-flow also supports multiple instances, while nullclaw has durable shared state and workspace files. Concurrent writes to the same repo or workspace can race and corrupt git state or files; the overlap is direct and dangerous by default if co-located.
conditions: IF both agents operate in the same repository or workspace, concurrent git and filesystem writes can conflict.
IF the orchestrator does not serialize MCP or shell actions, race conditions can corrupt shared state.
mitigations: Assign each agent a separate working directory.
Pause one agent before the other writes git state.
Use file locks around shared artifacts.
Review and merge git changes manually before commit.
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level locking for filesystem and git operations.

D_cascading_error.rationale: agentic-flow’s hooks/workers and MCP-driven workflow can consume outputs from nullclaw, which itself can browse, transcribe, and handle webhook payloads. That makes it plausible for one agent’s output to become the other’s input without a verification step. The pair is not documented as a verified pipeline, so medium fits the inferred cascade risk.
conditions: IF nullclaw-generated text is fed into agentic-flow workers without validation, errors can propagate downstream.
IF agentic-flow acts on webhook or browser-derived facts from nullclaw, mistaken outputs can cascade.
mitigations: Insert a human review step before downstream actions.
Require structured outputs with schema validation.
Compare critical facts against a second source before acting.
Log source provenance on every handoff.
requires-engineering: add confidence thresholds and rejection paths for low-trust inputs.

E_compliance.rationale: nullclaw explicitly handles API keys, private keys, bearer tokens, and audit logs, while agentic-flow touches repository metadata, code, and task prompts and has allowlisted egress. If regulated or sensitive data is placed into the pair, retention and residency controls may diverge across the two open-source stacks. The profiles do not prove a specific jurisdiction mismatch, so medium is the safest supported level.
conditions: IF sensitive credentials or regulated records are stored in nullclaw’s workspace and then processed by agentic-flow, retention obligations may diverge.
IF either deployment logs prompts or workspace files differently, deletion/export requests may be incomplete.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of shared workspaces.
Document retention settings for both agents.
Disable verbose logging for sensitive sessions.
Review where audit logs are stored and who can access them.
requires-engineering: align residency, retention, and deletion workflows across both deployments.
